consensus_summary: Biblical liberty primarily denotes spiritual freedom from bondage to sin, death, and the law’s condemnation through Christ, enabling holiness and loving service rather than license or autonomy.
book_summary: Liberty is the King’s jubilee release from bondage to sin into God’s household, inheritance, and faithful service; it changes masters rather than abolishing authority and is neither license to sin nor freedom from the law’s obligations.
consensus_core_identification: spiritual freedom from sin/death/law-condemnation in Christ for service
book_core_identification: King’s jubilee release from sin-bondage into God’s household/inheritance/service (master-change)
boundary_disagreement: Book tightly binds liberty to Jubilee typology, household/inheritance transfer, and continued law-obligations under a new master; consensus admits broader emphases (freedom from Mosaic yoke as justification, conscience/adiaphora, eschatological liberation) while still rejecting license.
material_contradiction: None; both reject libertinism and affirm service under God, differing only in framing precision and boundary stress on law-obligations versus freedom from the law’s condemning yoke.
rationale: Minimum cores identify the same Christ-won release from sin into righteous service. Book preserves that referent but refines extension and conditions via explicit Jubilee/King/household language and the insistence that authority and law-obligations remain, narrowing cases the broader consensus leaves open.
strongest_objection: Printed citations foreground Jubilee and ‘law of liberty’/anti-license texts while omitting the dominant NT eleutheria passages (Gal 5; Rom 6–8; John 8; 2 Cor 3) that anchor the consensus primary meaning.
